vocabulary.definition: Day of the Three Kings (Epiphany) - January 6

timeline.event: Our Lady of Guadalupe appeared to Juan Diego in Mexico.
Christopher Columbus brought Spanish language and Catholic faith to the Americas.
Father Junípero Serra founded the first California mission in San Diego.
California became a state with many Spanish missions and Spanish-speaking Catholics.

artworks.title: Our Lady of Guadalupe
artworks.description: An image of Mary appearing to Juan Diego, wearing a blue-green cloak covered with stars, standing on a crescent moon with an angel below.

artworks.title: Las Posadas Procession
artworks.description: People carrying candles walking through streets at night, with children dressed as Mary and Joseph seeking shelter.

artworks.title: Mexican Nativity Scene
artworks.description: Colorful handmade figures showing the Baby Jesus, Mary, Joseph, shepherds, animals, and the Three Kings around a simple stable.

artworks.title: Day of the Dead Altar
artworks.description: A decorated table with photographs, marigold flowers, candles, sugar skulls, and favorite foods to remember loved ones who have died.

artworks.title: Three Kings Day Celebration
artworks.description: Three wise men in crowns and robes riding camels, carrying gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh, following a bright star.

artworks.title: Holy Week Procession in Spain
artworks.description: People in traditional robes carrying religious statues and crosses through city streets during Semana Santa.

artworks.title: Mission Church Bells
artworks.description: White adobe church with a bell tower, red tile roof, and arched doorways at a California mission.

artworks.title: La Virgen de Guadalupe Tilma
artworks.description: The original image preserved in Mexico City showing Mary's appearance to Juan Diego on his cloak made of cactus fiber.

locations.name: Mexico
locations.significance: The largest Spanish-speaking country where many Catholic traditions like Las Posadas and Día de los Muertos originated.

locations.name: Spain
locations.significance: The country where the Spanish language comes from and where many Catholic Holy Week traditions are celebrated.

locations.name: Basilica of Our Lady of Guadalupe (Mexico City)
locations.significance: The church built where Mary appeared to Juan Diego, one of the most visited Catholic pilgrimage sites in the world.

locations.name: California Missions
locations.significance: 21 missions founded by Spanish priests where Catholic faith and Spanish language were taught.

locations.name: Vatican City
locations.significance: The home of the Pope and center of the Catholic Church, where Latin and many languages including Spanish are used.

locations.name: Bethlehem
locations.significance: The birthplace of Jesus, celebrated at Christmas (Navidad) in Spanish-speaking countries.

locations.name: Jerusalem
locations.significance: The holy city where Jesus died and rose again, remembered during Semana Santa and Pascua.

locations.name: Latin America
locations.significance: The region including Mexico, Central and South America where Spanish is spoken and Catholic faith is widely practiced.

trueFalse.statement: Navidad is the Spanish word for Christmas.
trueFalse.correction: Spanish-speaking families celebrate Navidad with special traditions like Las Posadas, nativity scenes (belenes), and special foods.

trueFalse.statement: Las Posadas celebrates Easter.
trueFalse.correction: Las Posadas is a nine-day Christmas celebration from December 16-24 that reenacts Mary and Joseph's search for shelter in Bethlehem.

trueFalse.statement: Día de los Reyes Magos is celebrated on January 6.
trueFalse.correction: This day celebrates when the Three Wise Men brought gifts to Baby Jesus. In Spanish-speaking countries, children often receive gifts on this day instead of Christmas.

trueFalse.statement: Semana Santa means 'Happy Week.'
trueFalse.correction: Semana Santa means 'Holy Week' - the week before Easter when Catholics remember Jesus' death and resurrection.

trueFalse.statement: Our Lady of Guadalupe appeared to Juan Diego in Mexico in 1531.
trueFalse.correction: Mary appeared to Juan Diego on Tepeyac Hill near Mexico City. Her image miraculously appeared on his cloak and is still preserved today.

trueFalse.statement: Día de los Muertos is a sad day when families are afraid of death.
trueFalse.correction: Día de los Muertos (Day of the Dead) is a joyful celebration on November 2 when families remember and honor loved ones who have died, believing they are in heaven with God.

trueFalse.statement: Cuaresma is the Spanish word for Lent.
trueFalse.correction: Cuaresma is the 40-day period before Easter when Catholics pray, fast, and prepare their hearts for Pascua (Easter).

trueFalse.statement: In Spanish, 'Dios' means 'day.'
trueFalse.correction: 'Dios' means 'God' in Spanish. The word for 'day' is 'día.' Spanish-speaking Catholics pray to Dios and attend church (iglesia).

trueFalse.statement: Villancicos are Spanish Christmas carols.
trueFalse.correction: Villancicos are joyful songs sung during the Christmas season in Spanish-speaking countries, often about the birth of Jesus.

trueFalse.statement: Miércoles de Ceniza is the last day of Lent.
trueFalse.correction: Miércoles de Ceniza (Ash Wednesday) is the FIRST day of Lent, when Catholics receive ashes on their foreheads as a sign of repentance.

trueFalse.statement: The rosario is a Spanish prayer using beads.
trueFalse.correction: The rosario (rosary) is a special Catholic prayer honoring Mary. Spanish-speaking Catholics often pray the rosary together as families.

trueFalse.statement: Nochebuena is celebrated on December 31.
trueFalse.correction: Nochebuena (literally 'Good Night') is Christmas Eve, December 24, when many Spanish-speaking families attend midnight Mass and have a special meal.

trueFalse.statement: Saint Joseph is called 'San José' in Spanish.
trueFalse.correction: San José is Spanish for Saint Joseph, the earthly father of Jesus. Many churches, cities, and missions are named after him.

trueFalse.statement: Spanish-speaking Catholics celebrate All Saints' Day on November 1.
trueFalse.correction: Día de Todos los Santos (All Saints' Day) honors all the saints in heaven and is celebrated the day before Día de los Muertos.

trueFalse.statement: A 'belén' is a type of Spanish food eaten at Christmas.
trueFalse.correction: A belén (also called nacimiento) is a nativity scene showing the birth of Jesus with Mary, Joseph, and the Baby Jesus in the manger.

trueFalse.statement: The word 'ángel' means 'angel' in Spanish.
trueFalse.correction: Angels (ángeles) are important in Catholic faith. The Angel Gabriel announced Jesus' birth to Mary, and angels appeared to the shepherds.

trueFalse.statement: Adviento is the season of preparation before Christmas.
trueFalse.correction: Adviento (Advent) is the four-week season before Christmas when Catholics prepare their hearts to celebrate Jesus' birth through prayer and waiting.

trueFalse.statement: Pascua refers to Thanksgiving in Spanish.
trueFalse.correction: Pascua is Easter, the most important celebration in the Catholic Church when we remember that Jesus rose from the dead.

trueFalse.statement: Fe, esperanza, and caridad are the three theological virtues.
trueFalse.correction: These Spanish words mean faith, hope, and charity (love) - the three main virtues that help us grow closer to God.

trueFalse.statement: The Spanish missions in California were founded to teach Catholic faith.
trueFalse.correction: Spanish priests like Father Junípero Serra founded 21 missions to share the Catholic faith and teach Spanish to Native Americans.
